name: Gore Place

dates.note: The HABS addendum quotes the National Historic Landmark website's 'Built in 1805-06'; SAH Archipedia gives 1805-1806 with Rebecca Gore and Jacques G. Legrand; the Wikipedia infobox prints 'Built 1804-1806'; the node's exemplar year is 1806. None edited to agree.

survey.prepared: Addendum, undated on the extracted span; it cites the National Historic Landmark website 'accessed 22 December 2013' and a coordinate 'obtained using Google Earth on 22 December 2013'

quotes.text: Statement of Significance: From the National Historic Landmark website: “Built in 1805-06, this is a noteworthy example of a five-part Federal house. Elaborately carved interior mantels contrast with simpler woodwork. In addition, Gore Place is nationally significant as representative of the central role of domestic labor in American labor history.
quotes.page: HABS MA-210 addendum; no page marker legible in the extract span

quotes.text: Due to the incomplete nature of the documentation and the lack of field measurements to verify the drawings, the drawings may not meet HABS standards and have been marked as such. Most of these drawings are still in pencil, that combined with the age of the drawings, presented challenges when digitizing them, so the scanned images are not as clear as most of the drawings within the HABS collection.
quotes.page: HABS MA-210 addendum; no page marker legible in the extract span

note: Written 4 Sep 2026. The written data is a 2013 addendum wrapping unfinished 1930s pencil drawings that the addendum itself says 'may not meet HABS standards' for want of field measurements -- so the Library holds no verified dimensions for this house, and the node's 'roughly 190 feet long' stays the node's. `new-england-federal` also names the building; see the Otis House note.
